KEY MESSAGE 1...

In the mid/upper-levels, an amplifying subtropical ridge was 
centered over the central Rocky Mountains, with a well-defined 
shortwave trough pivoting across south-central Canada and into 
western Ontario. A closed, mid-level low was embedded within this 
shortwave trough, the latter of which is on the western periphery of 
a larger-scale belt of cyclonic, gyre-like flow over northeastern 
Canada. The exit-region to the anticyclonic jet streak arcing over 
the center of the subtropical ridge was overspreading the region, 
with anvil debris/mare's tails advecting towards the western 
portions of the CWA. As such, large-scale subsidence will result 
keep the bubbling cu field suppressed this afternoon, with the 
exception of the mountains due to the typical orographic effects.

At the surface, a warm front was nearly stalled to the south of the 
CWA along the NC/TN/VA border, with WAA-induced showers ongoing 
along the spine of the Cumberland Mountains in far western VA and 
into far southern Coal Fields. This warm front will continue to 
sharpen in baroclinity while advecting poleward over the next 24 
hours in response to the large-scale pressure falls associated with 
the aforementioned shortwave trough digging into the Great Lakes 
region by dawn Tuesday. Widely-scattered showers and storms may 
develop across the mountainous terrain for the remainder of the 
afternoon hours, as the warm front will be slow to advect poleward 
until later tonight. Severe weather is not expected this afternoon; 
however, highly localized flash flooding will be possible given the 
meager CAPE profiles of <=1,075 J/kg (per 12Z RAOB from WFO RNK) and 
PWATs between 1.00-1.25". Otherwise, muggy conditions are expected 
area-wide for the rest of today beneath a high-altitude smoke plume, 
the latter of which may result in some reductions to visibility, 
primarily across the northern portions of the CWA.

As the warm front continues to lift poleward during overnight hours, 
WAA-induced showers and perhaps a couple of storms may develop along 
the leading edge of the front. Convective organization will be 
greatly tempered, with cells progressing northeastward in tandem 
with the warm front. Brief downpours will be possible, with PoPs 
maintained across the mountainous terrain across WV southwestward 
into far western VA. It is possible that showers linger into sunrise 
across those locales as the leading wave of shortwave perturbations 
begin to eject over the CWA. Severe weather is not expected tonight.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

Widespread showers and storms are forecast area-wide Tuesday, as the 
shortwave trough currently digging into western Ontario begins to 
eject over the Great Lakes while becoming open. The opening of the 
closed low will be induced by another more-subtle shortwave trough 
digging south-southeastward over the Hudson Bay, which will act to 
maintain the progressiveness of the mean troughing. Geopotential 
height falls on the order of about 30 m/12 hr will contribute to a 
net increase in thermal instability, with CAPE values ranging 
between 1,500-2,500 J/kg, depending on parcel trajectory. The 12Z 
RAOB from INL this past morning sampled the elevated mixed layer 
advecting eastward towards the region, with MUCAPE of 2,252 J/kg, 
which bolsters confidence in the handling of the EML by forecast 
soundings. A decaying MCS generated during the previous night is 
forecast to propagate across the Rust Belt and into southeastern OH 
by daybreak Tuesday, which may result in substantial convective 
overturning of the airmass as its remnants propagate across the CWA 
through the late morning hours. Thick anvil debris and intermittent 
heavy showers may inhibit the vigor of convection by the afternoon, 
as successful recovery of the airmass is uncertain despite effective 
and cloud-layer shear magnitudes increasing to 50 kt and 60 kt, 
respectively. However, areas that are not affected by the remnant 
MCS for a prolonged period of time will have the greatest potential 
for airmass recovery, and there is particular interest across the 
southwestern zones where this may come to fruition. 

Differential diabatic heating through cloud breaks amidst moderate 
return flow will aid in boosting temperatures into the upper 80s, 
contributing to a strongly unstable boundary-layer by the afternoon 
hours as dewpoints hold steady in the lower-middle 70s. As the 
synoptic cold front approaches from the northwest and convective 
temperatures are reached, rapid storm development will be possible 
across the Coal Fields of northeastern KY and into southwestern WV, 
with storms forecast to unzip into another MCS that should become 
organized quickly due to the magnitude of large-scale forcing for 
ascent. Corfidi vectors favor upshear propagation of cellular 
development as the cold pool(s) of the MCS establish, with MCS
